lessons.title: Fractions: add, subtract, multiply
steps: To add or subtract fractions, the bottom numbers (denominators) must be the same. Find a common denominator first.
Change each fraction so it has that denominator, then add or subtract only the top numbers (numerators).
To multiply fractions, multiply the tops together and the bottoms together. Then simplify.

lessons.title: Decimals: add, subtract, multiply
steps: When you add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points. Add zeros if it helps.
Work from the right, like normal numbers, and keep the decimal point in the same place in the answer.
To multiply decimals, multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places in both numbers together.

examples.a: 4 x 3 = 12. There are 2 decimal places in total, so 0.12.

lessons.title: Percentages
steps: Percent means out of 100. 25% means 25 out of 100.
To find a percentage of an amount, divide the amount by 100, then multiply by the percentage.
To change a fraction to a percentage, make the bottom 100, or multiply the fraction by 100.

examples.q: A shirt costs MK 2000. It has 10% off. What is the new price?
